1167.text: The heat of neutralization of a strong base and a strong acid is $57 \mathrm{~kJ}$. The heat released when 0.5 mole of $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ solution is added to 0.20 moles of $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution, is
1167.sol:
Heat of neutralization $(\Delta H)=57 \mathrm{~kJ}$, mole of $\mathrm{HNO}_3=0.5$ mole and mole of $\mathrm{NaOH}=0.2$ mole. When $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ solution is added to $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution, then 0.2 mole of $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ solution will combine with 0.2 mole of $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ions of $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution.
$\therefore \quad$ Heat released $=\Delta H \times 0.2=57 \times 0.2=11.4 \mathrm{~kJ}$.

Assertion : We cannot think of a magnetic field configuration with three poles.
Reason : A bar magnet does exert a torque on itself due to its own field.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.

If both assertion and reason are false.
1654.sol: Magnetic poles always exist in pairs. However, one can imagine magnetic field configuration with three poles. 1988.subject: Zoology
1988.text:
Assertion : ADH and RAAS work in response to low blood volume and blood pressure. 
Reason: ANF works in response to high blood volume and blood pressure.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
1988.sol:
ADH (Antidiuretic hormone) and RAAS (Renin Angiotensin Aldosterone System) work in response to low blood volume and low blood pressure. $\mathrm{ADH}$ increases the reabsorption of water in the distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct and thus results in an increase in blood volume and blood pressure. RAAS is operated by JGA (Juxtaglomerular apparatus). It increases blood volume and blood pressure by two ways: Firstly, it induces the proximal convoluted tubules to reabsorb more $\mathrm{NaCl}$ and water and secondly, it stimulates the adrenal glands to release a hormone, called aldosterone that induces the distal convoluted tubule to absorb more $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$and water.
ANF (Atrial Natriuretic Factor) works in response to high blood volume and high blood pressure. It opposes the regulation by RAAS. The walls of the atria of the heart release ANF in response to an increase in blood volume and blood pressure. ANF inhibits release of renin from the JGA and thereby inhibits $\mathrm{NaCl}$ reabsorption by the collecting duct and reduces aldosterone release from the adrenal gland. Thus $\mathrm{ADH}$, RAAS and ANF regulate the functions of kidneys and control body fluid osmolarity, salt concentration, blood pressure and blood volume.
1988.meta: Assertion : ADH and RAAS work in response to low blood volume and blood pressure. Reason: ANF works in response to high blood volume and blood pressure.

3286.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
3286.text: Higher second ionisation enthalpies than expected are observed for
3286.sol:
The electronic configuration of $\mathrm{Cr}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^5 4 s^1$ and that of $\mathrm{Cu}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^{10} 4 s^1$. Their second ionisation enthalpies are higher than expected because after removal of one electron chromium gets a half-filled electronic configuration and $\mathrm{Cu}$ get a fully-filled $3 d$ electronic configuration. These configuration are more stable than the partial-filled electronic configuration. So, it is very difficult to remove the second electron in both cases.
Thus, option (d) is correct.

So $ f^{\prime}(0)$ is finite and exists if \alpha>1\Rightarrow f(x)$ is differentiable at $x=0$ if \alpha>$1$.

16554.text: A calorimeter contains \(0.5 $\mathrm{ kg}$\) of water at \(30^{{}^{\circ}} $\mathrm{C}$\). 16554.sol:
Temperature of cold water in calorimeter,
$T_1=30^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}, m_1=0.5 \mathrm{ kg}=500 \mathrm{ g}\)
Temperature$ of $hot water, \(T_2=60^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}\),
\(m_2=0.3 \mathrm{ kg}=300 \mathrm{ g}\)
Resulting temperature, \(T_3=40^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}\)
Let water equivalent of the calorimeter is \(W_{\text{gram }}\).
According to principle of calorimetry.
Heat lost by warm water \(=\) Heat gained by cold water + Heat gained by the calorimeter
\begin{aligned}& \Rightarrow \quad m_2\left(T_2-T_3\right)=m_1\left(T_3-T_1\right)+W\left(T_3-T_1\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 300(60-40)=500(40-30)+W(40-30) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 300 \times20=500 \times10+10 W \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 6000=5000+10 W \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 10 W=6000-5000 \Rightarrow 10 W=1000 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad W=100 \mathrm{ g}=\frac{100}{1000}=0.1 \mathrm{ kg}
\end{aligned}$

The resultant amplitude of waves at the point $P$ is, A = $\sqrt{{A}_{1}^{2} + {A}_{2}^{2} + 2{A}_{1}{A}_{2}cosϕ} Here, $ϕ$is the phase difference and ${A}_{1}$\text{and}${A}_{2}$ are amplitude of sound waves.

18089.text: For each parabola $y=x^2+p x+q$, meeting coordinate axes at 3-distinct points, if circles are drawn through these points, then the family of circles must pass through
18089.sol:
Suppose the parabola $y=x^2+p x+q$ cuts $X$-axis at $A(\alpha, 0)$ and $B(\beta, 0)$.
Then, $\alpha, \beta$ are roots of the equation $x^2+p x+q=0
\therefore \quad \alpha+\beta=-$ p $\text{ and } \alpha \beta=$ q

The parabola $y=x^2+p x+q$ cuts $Y$-axis at $(0, q)$.
Let the equation of the circle passing through $A, B$ and $C$ be

$\begin{aligned}$& x²+y²+2 g x+2 f y+c  =0 &...(i)\\
\therefore  $\alpha^2+2 g \alpha+$ c  =0 &...(ii)\\
 $\beta^2+2 g \beta+$ c  =0 &...(iii)\\
$\text{ and }$& q²+2 f q+c  =0 &...(iv)
\end{aligned}

Subtracting Eq. (iii) from Eq. (ii), we get

$\begin{array}{rlrl}\alpha+\beta+2 g & =0 \\
\Rightarrow & g = p / 2
\end{array}

Adding Eqs. (ii) and (iii), we get

\begin{array}{r}\alpha^2+\beta^2+2 g(\alpha+\beta)+2 c=0 \\
(\alpha+\beta)^2-2 \alpha \beta+2 g(\alpha+\beta)+2 c=0 \\
p²-2 q-p²+2 c=0
\end{array}

\left[\because \alpha+\beta=$ p $\text{ and }$ g=$\frac{p}{2}\right]$ Putting $c=q$ in Eq. (iv), we get $f=- \left(\frac{q+1}{2}\right)
Substituting the values of $g, f$ and $c$ in Eq. (i), we obtain the equation of family of circles passing through $A, B$ and $C$ as

x^2+y^2+p x-(q+1) y+q=0

Clearly, it passes through $(0,1)$.$

18693.subject: Mathematics
18693.text: The image of the point $( 1, 6, 3 )$ in the line $\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 2}{3}$ is
18693.sol:
Let $P ( 1, 6, 3 )$ be the given point and $L$ be the foot of perpendicular from $P$ to the given line. The coordinates of a general point on the given line are

$\dfrac{x - 0}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 2}{3} = \lambda$ & (say)

i.e. $x = \lambda$

$y = 2\lambda + 1, z = 3\lambda + 2$

If the coordinates of $L$ are $( \lambda, 2\lambda + 1, 3\lambda + 2 )$, then the direction ratios of $PL$ are $( \lambda - 1, 2\lambda - 5, 3\lambda - 1 )$.

Since, the direction ratios of given line which is perpendicular to $PL$, are $1, 2$ and $3$. Therefore, $( \lambda - 1 ) 1 + ( 2\lambda - 5 ) 2 + ( 3\lambda - 1 )^{3} = 0$,which gives $\lambda = 1$.

Hence, coordinates of $L$ are $( 1, 3, 5 )$.

Let $Q \left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}, {z}_{1}\right) be the image of $P ( 1, 6, 3 )$ in the given line. Then, $L$ is the mid-point of $PQ$.

Therefore, \dfrac{{x}_{1} + 1}{2} =1, \dfrac{{y}_{1} + 6}{2} =3, \dfrac{{z}_{1} + 3}{2} =5$

$⇒ {x}_{1} = 1, y = 0, z = 7$

Hence, the image of $( 1, 6, 3 )$ in the given line is $( 1, 0, 7 )$.

(3) Incorrect: Dipole moment of $NH_3$ is greater than that of $NF_3$. In $NH_3$, the lone pair dipole and N-H bond dipoles add up. In $NF_3$, the N-F bond dipoles oppose the lone pair dipole, partially canceling it.

(4) Correct: $AB_5E$ type has steric number 6 (octahedral electron geometry). With one lone pair occupying one position, the molecular geometry is square pyramidal (e.g., $BrF_5$, $IF_5$).

19867.subject: Chemistry
19867.text:
The rate constant for a zero order reaction $\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{B}+\mathrm{C}$ is $6.0 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{molL}^{-1} \mathrm{ s}^{-1}$.
What would be the time taken for the initial concentration of A to decrease from 0.2 M to 0.024 M ?
19867.sol:
For a zero order reaction, the integrated rate equation is given by $[A]_t = [A]_0 - kt$, where $[A]_0$ is the initial concentration, $[A]_t$ is the concentration at time $t$, and $k$ is the rate constant.

Given values are $[A]_0 = 0.2 \text{ M}$, $[A]_t = 0.024 \text{ M}$, and $k = 6.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol L}^{-1} \text{ s}^{-1}$.

Rearranging the equation to solve for $t$:

$t = \dfrac{[A]_0 - [A]_t}{k}$

Substituting the values:

$t = \dfrac{0.2 - 0.024}{6.0 \times 10^{-3}}$

$t = \dfrac{0.176}{6.0 \times 10^{-3}}$

$t = \dfrac{176}{6} \text{ s}$

$t = 29.333... \text{ s}$

Rounding to two decimal places, $t = 29.33 \text{ s}$.

Answer: 29.33 s

20125.subject: Chemistry
20125.text: What will be the change in the electrode potential of chromium electrode dipping into chromic sulphate solution, when the electrolyte is diluted 10 times at $25^{}^{\circ}$ C? [ $E^0\ (\text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr})] = -0.74$ V
20125.sol:
The reduction half-reaction for the chromium electrode is:

$\text{Cr}^{3+} + 3e^- \rightarrow \text{Cr}$

The Nernst equation for the reduction potential is given by:

$E = E^0 - \dfrac{0.0591}{n} \log \dfrac{1}{[\text{Cr}^{3+}]}$

$E = E^0 + \dfrac{0.0591}{3} \log [\text{Cr}^{3+}]$

Let the initial concentration of $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ be $c$. The initial electrode potential is:

$E_1 = E^0 + \dfrac{0.0591}{3} \log c$

When the solution is diluted 10 times, the new concentration becomes $\dfrac{c}{10}$$. The new electrode potential is:

$E_2 = E^0 + $\dfrac{0.0591}{3}$ $\log$$\left(\dfrac{c}{10}\right)<$ br>
The change in electrode potential is:

\Delta$ E = E_2 - E_1 = \dfrac{0.0591}{3}\left[ \log \$ left($\dfrac{c}{10}$\right) - \logc \right]$

\Delta E = \dfrac{0.0591}{3} \log\left(\dfrac{1}{10}\right)$

\Delta$ E = \dfrac{0.0591}{3} \times (-1) = -0.0197 \text{ V}

\Delta$ E = -19.7 $\text{ mV}$

The negative sign indicates that the electrode potential decreases by 19.7 $\text{ mV}$.

Answer: Decrease by 19.7 mV$

21042.subject: Mathematics
21042.text: If $49^{n}+16 n+P$ is divisible by 64 for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$, then the least negative integral value of $P$ is
21042.sol:
Let $f(n) = 49^{n} + 16n + P$. We are given that $f(n)$ is divisible by 64 for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

For $n = 1$, $f(1) = 49^{1} + 16(1) + P = 49 + 16 + P = 65 + P$.

For $f(1)$ to be divisible by 64, $65 + P = 64k$ for some integer $k$.

For $n = 2$, $f(2) = 49^{2} + 16(2) + P = 2401 + 32 + P = 2433 + P$.

For $f(2)$ to be divisible by 64, $2433 + P = 64m$ for some integer $m$.

Subtracting the two conditions: $(2433 + P) - (65 + P) = 64m - 64k$, which gives $2368 = 64(m - k)$.

Since $2368 / 64 = 37$, the condition is consistent for all $n$.

From $65 + P = 64k$, we have $P = 64k - 65$.

To find the least negative integral value of $P$, we test values of $k$.

If $k = 1$, $P = 64(1) - 65 = -1$.

If $k = 0$, $P = -65$.

If $k = 2$, $P = 64(2) - 65 = 128 - 65 = 63$.

The values of $P$ are of the form $64k - 65$. The negative values are $-1, -65, -129, \dots$.

The least negative integral value among the options provided is $-1$.

Answer: $-1$

21225.subject: Mathematics
options: $f$ is not continuous but differentiable at $x=1$
$f$ is continuous but not differentiable at $x=1$
21225.sol:
To check continuity at $x=1$, we evaluate the left-hand limit and right-hand limit.

Left-hand limit: $\lim_{x \to 1^{-}} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 1^{-}} x = 1$.

Right-hand limit: $\lim_{x \to 1^{+}} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 1^{+}} (2x - 1) = 2(1) - 1 = 1$.

Since $f(1) = 1$ and the limits are equal, $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=1$.

To check differentiability at $x=1$, we evaluate the left-hand derivative and right-hand derivative.

Left-hand derivative: $f'(1^{-}) = \dfrac{d}{dx}(x) = 1$.

Right-hand derivative: $f'(1^{+}) = \dfrac{d}{dx}(2x - 1) = 2$.

Since $f'(1^{-}) \neq f'(1^{+})$, the function is not differentiable at $x=1$.

Therefore, $f$ is continuous but not differentiable at $x=1$.

Answer: $f$ is continuous but not differentiable at $x=1$

21979.subject: Mathematics
21979.text: Every term of a geometric progression is positive, and every term is the sum of the two preceding terms. Then the common ratio of the geometric progression is:
21979.sol:
Let the geometric progression be $a, ar, ar^2, \dots$

Given that every term is positive, we have $a > 0$ and $r > 0$.

According to the given condition, every term is the sum of the two preceding terms.

$T_n = T_{n-1} + T_{n-2}$

For $n = 3$, we get:

$ar^2 = ar + a$

Dividing by $a$ (since $a > 0$):

$r^2 = r + 1$

$r^2 - r - 1 = 0$

Solving for $r$ using the quadratic formula:

$r = \dfrac{-(-1) \pm \sqrt{(-1)^2 - 4(1)(-1)}}{2}$

$r = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}$

Since $r > 0$, we reject $r = \dfrac{1 - \sqrt{5}}{2}$.

Therefore, the common ratio is $r = \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}$

22538.text: Two bodies of masses $1 \mathrm{ kg}$ and $2 \mathrm{ kg}$ have equal momentum. Then, the ratio of their kinetic energies is
22538.sol:
Let $m_{1}$ be the mass of 1 st body , $m_{1}=1 \mathrm{ kg}m_{2}$ be the mass of $2 \mathrm{nd}$ body, $m_{2}=2 \mathrm{ kg}$

22903.subject: Physics
22903.text: The radius of earth is $R$ and acceleration due to gravity on its surface is $g$. The height at which the acceleration due to gravity becomes $\dfrac{g}{8}$ is:
22903.sol:
The acceleration due to gravity at a height $h$ above the surface of the Earth is given by the formula $g' = g \left( \dfrac{R}{R+h} \right)^{2}$, where $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity at the surface and $R$ is the radius of the Earth.

Given that $g' = \dfrac{g}{8}$, we substitute this into the equation:

$\dfrac{g}{8} = g \left( \dfrac{R}{R+h} \right)^{2}$

Dividing both sides by $g$ gives:

$\dfrac{1}{8} = \left( \dfrac{R}{R+h} \right)^{2}$

Taking the square root of both sides:

$\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{R}{R+h}$

Rearranging the terms to solve for $h$:

$R + h = 2\sqrt{2} R$

$h = 2\sqrt{2} R - R$

$h = (2\sqrt{2} - 1) R$

Answer: $(2 \sqrt{2}-1) R$

24632.text:
The periodic table consists of 18 groups. An isotope of copper, on bombardment with protons, undergoes a nuclear reaction yielding element $X$ as shown below. To which group, element $X$ belongs in the periodic table?

${ }_{29}^{63} \mathrm{Cu}+{ }_{1}^{1} \mathrm{H} \rightarrow 6_{0}^{1} n+{ }_{2}^{4} \alpha+2{ }_{1}^{1} \mathrm{H}+\mathrm{X}$
24632.sol:
${ }_{29}^{63} \mathrm{Cu}+{ }_{1}^{1} \mathrm{H} \rightarrow 6{ }_{0}^{1} n+{ }_{2}^{4} \mathrm{He}+2{ }_{1}^{1} \mathrm{H}+{ }_{Z}^{A} X$

Balancing the atomic mass and atomic number

$63+1=(6 \times 1)+4+2+A \Rightarrow A=52$

$29+1=(6 \times 0)+2+2+Z \Rightarrow Z=26$

Thus ${ }_{Z}^{A} X={ }_{26}^{52} X$ or ${ }_{26}^{52} \mathrm{Fe}$

Hence, $X$ belongs to group 8 in the periodic table.

27191.subject: Chemistry
27191.text:
Consider the following reactions sequence

When the product (P) is subjected to Carius analysis using $AgNO_3$, $1.0$ g of the product (P) will produce _______ g of the precipitate of AgBr. (Nearest Integer)
(Given: molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ C : 12, H : 1, O : 16, N : 14, Br : 80, Ag : 108)
27191.sol:
The given reactant is p-nitrotoluene.

Step (i): Reduction with Sn/HCl followed by $OH^-$ converts the $-NO_2$ group to an $-NH_2$ group, yielding p-toluidine.

Step (ii): Reaction with acetic anhydride, $(CH_3CO)_2O$, protects the amino group by forming N-(4-methylphenyl)acetamide.

Step (iii): Bromination with $Br_2/AlBr_3$ directs the incoming bromine to the ortho position relative to the strongly activating $-NHCOCH_3$ group (the para position is blocked by the methyl group). This yields 2-bromo-4-methylacetanilide.

Step (iv): Acid hydrolysis with $H_3O^+$ removes the acetyl group, yielding 2-bromo-4-methylaniline as the major product (P).

The molecular formula of product P (2-bromo-4-methylaniline) is $C_7H_8NBr$.
Molar mass of P = $(7 \times 12) + (8 \times 1) + 14 + 80 = 186 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

In Carius analysis, the bromine in the organic compound is quantitatively converted to silver bromide (AgBr).
Molar mass of AgBr = $108 + 80 = 188 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

Since one molecule of P contains one bromine atom, 1 mole of P produces 1 mole of AgBr.
Moles of P in $1.0 \text{ g} = \dfrac{1.0}{186} \text{ mol}$.
Moles of AgBr produced = $\dfrac{1.0}{186} \text{ mol}$.
Mass of AgBr produced = $\dfrac{1.0}{186} \times 188 \text{ g} \approx 1.01 \text{ g}$.

Rounding to the nearest integer, the mass of the AgBr precipitate is 1 g.

Answer: $1$

29142.subject: Chemistry
29142.text: Which of the following $3d - metal$ ion will give the lowest enthalpy of hydration $\left({\Delta}_{hyd}H\right)$ when dissolved in water?
29142.sol:
Hydration enthalpy (ꕔHHyd) is the change in enthalpy when one mole of gaseous ion under a standard condition of 1 bar pressure dissolves in a sufficient amount of water to form an infinitely dilute solution (infinite dilution means a further addition of solute will not cause any heat change).

Hydration enthalpy is inversely related to the size of the ion, smaller the size of the ion greater is the hydration and hence greater is the hydration energy released.

Mn+2 has the lowest hydration energy among the given ions as it has the largest size.

Ion ${\Delta H}_{Hyd .}^{o} ( kJ / mole )$
${Cr}^{2 +}$ $- 1925$
${Mn}^{2 +}$ $- 1862$
${Fe}^{2 +}$ $- 1998$
${Co}^{2 +}$ $- 2079$

32888.text: Let $f: R \to R$ and $g: R \to R$ be two functions defined by $f\left(x\right) = {\log}_{e}\left({x}^{2} + 1\right) - {e}^{- x} + 1$ and $g\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1 - 2{e}^{2x}}{{e}^{x}} \cdot$ Then, for which of the following range of $\alpha$, the inequality $f\left(g\left(\dfrac{{\left(\alpha - 1\right)}^{2}}{3}\right)\right) > f\left(g\left(\alpha - \dfrac{5}{3}\right)\right)$ holds?
32888.sol:
$f\left(x\right) = {\log}_{e}\left({x}^{2} + 1\right) - {e}^{- x} + 1 ⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2x}{{x}^{2} + 1} + {e}^{- x} > 0, ∀ x \in R$

So $f\left(x\right)$ increasing

$g\left(x\right) = {e}^{- x} - 2{e}^{x} ⇒ {g}^{'}\left(x\right) = - \left({e}^{- x} + 2{e}^{x}\right) < 0 ∀ x \in R$

So $g\left(x\right)$ decreasing

$⇒ f\left(g\left(x\right)\right)$ is decreasing

$⇒ f\left(g\left(\dfrac{( \alpha - 1{)}^{2}}{3}\right)\right) > f\left(g\left(\alpha - \dfrac{5}{3}\right)\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\left(\alpha - 1\right)}^{2}}{3} < \alpha - \dfrac{5}{3}$

$⇒ \left(\alpha - 2\right)\left(\alpha - 3\right) < 0 ⇒ \alpha \in \left(2, 3\right)$

34159.text: If $24 \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\left(\sin \left|4 x-\frac{\pi}{12}\right|+[2 \sin x]\right) \mathrm{d} x=2 \pi+\alpha$, where $[\cdot]$ denotes the greatest integer function, then $\alpha$ is equal to _______.
34159.sol:
Let $I=24 \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\sin \left|4 x-\frac{\pi}{2}\right|+[2 \sin x]\right) d x$   ...(i)
Now $\left|4 x-\frac{\pi}{12}\right|= \begin{cases}-4 x+\frac{\pi}{12} & ; x < \frac{\pi}{48} \\ 4 x-\frac{\pi}{12} & ; \quad x \geq \frac{\pi}{48}\end{cases} \therefore$ from $(\mathrm{i}) \begin{aligned} & I=24 \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{48}}-\sin \left(4 x-\frac{\pi}{12}\right) d x+\int_{\frac{\pi}{48}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \sin \left(4 x-\frac{\pi}{12}\right) \\ & +\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{6}}[2 \sin x] d x+\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}[2 \sin x] d x \\ & I=24\left[\frac{\left(1-\cos \frac{\pi}{12}\right)}{4}-\frac{\left(-\cos \frac{\pi}{12}-1\right)}{4}\right)+\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{\pi}{6} \\ & I=24\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{\pi}{6} \\ & I=2 \pi+12=2 \pi+\alpha \text{ (from above) } \\ & \therefore \quad \alpha=12\end{aligned}$

34573.subject: Mathematics
34573.text:
If the system of linear equations
$x - 2y + kz = 1$
$2x + y + z = 2$
$3x - y - kz = 3$
has a solution $\left(x, y, z\right), z \ne 0,$ then $\left(x, y\right)$ lies on the straight line whose equation is:
34573.sol:
$x - 2y + kz = 1$ .........(1)
$2x + y + z = 2$ .........(2)
$3x - y - kz = 3$ ........(3)

Hence,

$\left[\begin{cases}1 & - 2 & k \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & - 1 & - k\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}x \\ y \\ z\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{array}\right]$

For infinite solution,

$\left|\begin{cases}1 & - 2 & k \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & - 1 & - k\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left(- k + 1\right) + 2\left(- 2k - 3\right) + k\left(- 2 - 3\right) = 0$

$⇒ k = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

Put this value in the equation $\left(1\right)$, we get

$2x - 4y - z = 2 . . . . \left(4\right)$

Adding the equation $\left(4\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$, we get

$4x - 3y = 4$

Hence, the equation of straight line is $4x - 3y - 4 = 0$

35211.text: Let $f: R \to R$ be a continuous function such that $f\left(3x\right) - f\left(x\right) = x$. If $f\left(8\right) = 7$, then $f\left(14\right)$ is equal to:
35211.sol:
Given $f\left(3x\right) - f\left(x\right) = x$

Now replance $x\text{by}\dfrac{x}{3}$ infinite times,

$f\left(x\right) - f\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) = \dfrac{x}{3}$

$f\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) - f\left(\dfrac{x}{{3}^{2}}\right) = \dfrac{x}{{3}^{2}} . .$

On adding, we get

$f\left(x\right) - \lim_{n \to \infty}f\left(\dfrac{x}{{3}^{n}}\right) = x\left(\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{{3}^{2}} + ⋯ + \infty\right)$

$f\left(x\right) - \lim_{n \to \infty}f\left(\dfrac{x}{{3}^{n}}\right) = x\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{3}}{1 - \dfrac{1}{3}}\right) = \dfrac{x}{2}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) - f\left(0\right) = \dfrac{x}{2}$

Given $f\left(8\right) = 7$

so $f\left(8\right) - f\left(0\right) = 4$

i.e. $f\left(0\right) = 3$

$∴ f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{2} + 3$

Hence $f\left(14\right) = 10$

36223.text: Let $S$ be the set of all $a \in N$ such that the area of the triangle formed by the tangent at the point $P\left(b, c\right), b, c \in N$,  on the parabola ${y}^{2} = 2ax$ and the lines $x = b, y = 0$ is $16{unit}^{2}$, then $\mathop{∑}_{a \in S}a$ is equal to _____ .
36223.sol:
Given,

$S$ be the set of all $a \in N$ such that the area of the triangle formed by the tangent at the point $P\left(b, c\right), b, c \in N$, on the parabola ${y}^{2} = 2ax$

And the lines $x = b, y = 0$ is $16{unit}^{2}$

Now plotting the diagram we get,

Tangent at $P\left(b, c\right)$ will be $ax - cy + ab = 0$ and it meets $x$-axis at $\left(- b, 0\right)$

Now area of triangle $\left(PAB\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(2b\right)\left(c\right) = 16 ⇒ bc = 16$

So, $\left(b, c\right) = \left(1, 16\right), \left(2, 8\right), \left(4, 4\right), \left(8, 2\right), \left(16, 1\right)$ as both belongs to natural number,

Now $\left(b, c\right)$ lie on parabola hence satisfy it

${c}^{2} = 2ab ⇒ {c}^{2} = 2a\left(\dfrac{16}{c}\right) ⇒ a = \dfrac{{c}^{3}}{32}$

Now when possible value of $c$ is $c = 4, 8, 16 ⇒ a = 2, 16, 128$

Hence, $\mathop{∑}_{a \in S}a = 2 + 16 + 128 = 146$.

36600.text: A fair die is tossed repeatedly until a six is obtained. Let $X$ denote the number of tosses required and let $a = P ( X = 3 ) , b = P ( X \ge 3 )$ and $c =$ $P ( X \ge 6 ∣ X > 3 )$. Then $\dfrac{b + c}{a}$ is equal to
36600.sol:
$P\left(\text{getting}6\right) = \dfrac{1}{6}, P\left(\text{not getting}6\right) = \dfrac{5}{6}$

$⇒ a = P ( X = 3 )$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{5}{6} \times \dfrac{5}{6} \times \dfrac{1}{6}$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{25}{216} . . . \left(i\right)$

$⇒ b = P ( X \ge 3 )$

$⇒ b = \dfrac{5}{6} \times \dfrac{5}{6} \times \dfrac{1}{6} + {\left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right)}^{3} \cdot \dfrac{1}{6} + {\left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right)}^{4} \cdot \dfrac{1}{6} + . . .$

We know that, ${S}_{\infty} = a + ar + {ar}^{2} + . . . \infty = \dfrac{a}{1 - r}$

$⇒ b = \dfrac{\dfrac{25}{216}}{1 - \dfrac{5}{6}}$

$⇒ b = \dfrac{25}{216} \times \dfrac{6}{1}$

$⇒ b = \dfrac{25}{36} . . . \left(ii\right)$

Now, $P ( X \ge 6 ) = {\left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right)}^{5} \cdot \dfrac{1}{6} + {\left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right)}^{6} \cdot \dfrac{1}{6} + . . .$

$⇒ P ( X \ge 6 ) = \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right)}^{5} \cdot \dfrac{1}{6}}{1 - \dfrac{5}{6}}$

$⇒ P ( X \ge 6 ) = {\left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right)}^{5}$

$⇒ c = P\left(\dfrac{X \ge 6}{X > 3}\right) = \dfrac{P\left(\left(X \ge 6\right) ∩ \left(X > 3\right)\right)}{P\left(X > 3\right)} = \dfrac{P\left(X \ge 6\right)}{P\left(X > 3\right)} = \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right)}^{5}}{{\left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right)}^{3}}$

$⇒ c = \dfrac{25}{36} . . . \left(iii\right)$

Using $\left(i\right), \left(ii\right)\text{and}\left(iii\right)$,

$⇒ \dfrac{b + c}{a} = \dfrac{\dfrac{25}{36} + \dfrac{25}{36}}{\dfrac{25}{216}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{b + c}{a} = \dfrac{\dfrac{50}{36}}{\dfrac{25}{216}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{b + c}{a} = 12$

39026.text: Which level of the single ionized carbon has the same energy as the ground state energy of hydrogen atom?
39026.sol:
Energy of $H$ -atom is $E = - 13 . 6{Z}^{2} / {n}^{2}$ for $H$-atom $Z = 1$ and for ground state, $n = 1$

$⇒ E = - 13 . 6 \times \dfrac{{1}^{2}}{{1}^{2}} = - 13 . 6eV$

Now for carbon atom (single ionised), $Z = 6$

$E = - 13 . 6\dfrac{{Z}^{2}}{{n}^{2}} = - 13 . 6$ (given)

$⇒ {n}^{2} = {6}^{2} ⇒ n = 6$

39521.text: The equivalent resistance between the points $A$ and $B$ in the following circuit is $\frac{x}{5} \Omega$. The value of $x$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
39521.sol:
Using Kirchhoff's laws on the bridge circuit with resistances $6\Omega, 3\Omega, 3\Omega, 3\Omega, 6\Omega$ and applying a 1V test voltage:

From the loop equation:
$6i_1 + 3(2i_1 - i) = 3(i - i_1)$

$15i_1 = 6i \Rightarrow i_1 = \frac{2}{5}i$ ...(1)

From the second loop:
$3(i - i_1) + 6i_1 = 1$
$3i + 3i_1 = 1$

$\left(3 + \frac{6}{5}\right)i = 1$

$i = \frac{5}{21} A = \frac{1V}{R_{eq}}$

$R_{eq} = \frac{21}{5} = 4.2 \ \Omega$

39626.text: A student is provided with a variable voltage source $V$, a test resistor ${R}_{T} = 10Ω$, two identical galvanometers ${G}_{1}$ and ${G}_{2}$ and two additional resistors, ${R}_{1} = 10MΩ$ and ${R}_{2} = 0 . 001Ω$. For conducting an experiment to verify ohm's law, the most suitable circuit is:
39626.sol:
A galvanometer is a tool used to either detect or quantify an electric current. The movement of a magnetic needle or a coil in a magnetic field, which is an essential component of a galvanometer, typically indicates the current and its strength.

Depending up on the resistance and the connectivity in the circuit, galvanometer can be used either as voltmeter or as an ammeter.

Voltmeter should have very high resistance, while ammeter should be having very less resistance.

Hence, the high resistor ${R}_{1}$ should be connected in series with the galvanometer in order to measure the potential difference across the test resistor. Also, the low resistor ${R}_{2}$ should be connected in parallel with the galvanometer in order to measure the current across the test resistor.

Thus, this combination will work properly.

40871.subject: Physics
40871.text: A planet has double the mass of the earth. Its average density is equal to that of the earth. An object weighing $W$ on earth will weigh on that planet:
40871.sol:
The formula for acceleration due to gravity is

$g = \dfrac{GM}{{R}^{2}}$

Let the density of earth and planet be $ρ$, and the radius of the planet be $R '$. Let $R$ be the radius of the earth and $g$ be the acceleration due to gravity of earth and $g '$ be the acceleration due to gravity of planet.

So, the masses are

$M = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3}ρ . . . ( i )$

$M ' = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{\left(R '\right)}^{3}ρ . . . ( ii )$

So, $\dfrac{g '}{{g}^{}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{GM '}{R{'}^{2}}}{\dfrac{GM}{{R}^{2}}} = \dfrac{M '}{M}{\left(\dfrac{R}{R '}\right)}^{2} . . . ( iii )$

From equation (i) and (ii) we get $R ' = 2\dfrac{1}{3}R$

Substituting the value in equation (iii),

$\dfrac{g '}{g} = \left({2}^{1}\right)2\dfrac{- 2}{3} = 2\dfrac{1}{3}g$

Weight is given by $W ' = mg ' = 2\dfrac{1}{3}W$

Absolute work $= + 6J$

Therefore, required value of $W = 6J$

46429.text: A car moves from $X$ to $Y$ with a uniform speed $v_u$ and returns to $Y$ with a uniform speed $v_d$. The average speed for this round trip is
46429.sol:
Let $t_1$ and $t_2$ be times taken by the car to go from $X$ to $Y$ and then from $Y$ to $X$ respectively. Then, $t_1+t_2=\frac{X Y}{v_u}+\frac{X Y}{v_d}=X Y\left(\frac{v_u+v_d}{v_u v_d}\right)$
Total distance travelled
$=X Y+X Y=2 X Y$
Therefore, average speed of the car for this round trip is
$\begin{aligned} v_{\mathrm{av}} & =\frac{2 X Y}{X Y\left(\frac{v_u+v_d}{v_u v_d}\right)} \\ \text{ or } \quad v_{\mathrm{av}} & =\frac{2 v_u v_d}{v_u+v_d}\end{aligned}$

51777.text: If a 3-digit number is randomly chosen, what is the probability that either the number itself or some permutation of the number (which is a 3 -digit number) is divisible by 4 and 5 ?
51777.sol:
We need 3 -digit number which is divisible by $4 \ \text{ and } 5$ both.
i.e. their last two digits are
$00,20,40,60 \ \text{ and } 80$
Now, ending with 00 are '9'.
$\{100,200, \ldots \ldots, 900\}$
If digit repeat other than ' 0 ' then they are
$\{220,440,660,880\}$
but 220 numbers can be permuted according to the condition as $\{220,202\}$
So, there are ' 8 ' other favorable cases.
If the number have no digit repeated like 320.
320 can be permuted in 4 ways.
$\{302,230,320,203\}$
So, such numbers are $8 \times 4 \times 4=128$
Total favorable $=9+8+128=145$
So, required prob. $=\frac{145}{900}=\frac{29}{180}$

57160.subject: Chemistry
57160.text:
Which of the following is correct decreasing order of acidic strength for the compounds listed below?
I: p-chlorophenol, II: p-Cresol, III: p-nitrophenol, IV: p-methoxyphenol.
57160.sol:
Acidic strength of phenols is directly proportional to the stability of the phenoxide ion formed after losing a proton.

Electron-withdrawing groups stabilize the phenoxide ion through $-I$ and $-R$ effects, thereby increasing the acidic strength. Electron-donating groups destabilize the phenoxide ion through $+I$, $+H$, and $+R$ effects, thereby decreasing the acidic strength.

In p-nitrophenol (III), the $-NO_2$ group exerts strong $-R$ and $-I$ effects, making it the most acidic.

In p-chlorophenol (I), the $-Cl$ group exerts a $-I$ effect which dominates over its $+R$ effect, making it more acidic than phenol but less acidic than p-nitrophenol.

In p-cresol (II), the $-CH_3$ group exerts $+I$ and hyperconjugation ($+H$) effects, decreasing the acidic strength compared to phenol.

In p-methoxyphenol (IV), the $-OCH_3$ group exerts a strong $+R$ effect which dominates over its $-I$ effect, making it the least acidic.

Thus, the decreasing order of acidic strength is III > I > II > IV.

Answer: III > I > II > IV

59780.subject: Chemistry
59780.text: Which from following process does NOT results in coagulation?
options: by mixing two oppositely charged sols
59780.sol:
Coagulation is the aggregation of colloidal particles into larger masses that sediment, following destabilization of the sol. Electrophoresis induces coagulation via charge neutralization at electrodes, boiling disrupts stabilizing layers through thermal agitation, and mixing oppositely charged sols causes mutual neutralization. Adding excess solvent, however, generally stabilizes the sol by reducing particle collision frequencies and diluting coagulating electrolytes, rather than promoting aggregation.

Thus, adding excess solvent does not typically result in coagulation.

59860.subject: Chemistry
59860.text: Which of the following processes exhibits the decrease in internal energy of a system?
options: Isothermal expansion of an ideal gas.
Isothrmal compression of an ideal gas.
Adiabatic expansion of an ideal gas.
Adiabatic compression of an ideal gas
59860.sol:
According to the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta U = q + w$.

For an isothermal process, the temperature remains constant (\Delta T = 0$). Since the internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, \Delta U = 0$ for both isothermal expansion and compression.

For an adiabatic process, there is no heat exchange with the surroundings, so $q = 0$. The first law becomes $\Delta U = w$.

During adiabatic expansion, work is done by the gas on the surroundings, meaning $w < 0$. Consequently, $\Delta U < 0$, which indicates a decrease in the internal energy of the system.

During adiabatic compression, work is done on the gas, meaning $w > 0$, leading to an increase in internal energy.

Answer: Adiabatic expansion of an ideal gas.

59951.subject: Chemistry
59951.text: Calculate the change in internal energy of the system if 20 kJ of work is done on the system and it releases 10 kJ of heat in a particular reaction.
59951.sol:
The First Law of Thermodynamics gives the change in internal energy as $\Delta U = q + w$, where $q$ is heat added to the system and $w$ is work done on the system.

Heat released by the system corresponds to $q = -10\text{ kJ}$, while work done on the system gives $w = +20\text{ kJ}$.

Substituting these values yields $\Delta U = (-10\text{ kJ}) + (20\text{ kJ}) = 10\text{ kJ}$.

The internal energy increases by $10\text{ kJ}$, making B the correct answer.

64443.subject: Mathematics
64443.text: The angle between the lines $x=\mathrm{y}, \mathrm{z}=0$ and $\mathrm{y}=0, \mathrm{z}=0$ is
64443.sol:
The angle between two lines can be determined by the angle between their direction vectors.

Line $x=y$, $z=0$ has direction vector $\mathrm{d}_1 = \langle 1, 1, 0 \rangle$.

Line $y=0$, $z=0$ (the $x$-axis) has direction vector $\mathrm{d}_2 = \langle 1, 0, 0 \rangle$.

The cosine of the angle $\theta$ satisfies $\cos \theta = \frac{|\mathrm{d}_1 \cdot \mathrm{d}_2|}{\|\mathrm{d}_1\| \cdot \|\mathrm{d}_2\|}$.

Compute the dot product: $\mathrm{d}_1 \cdot \mathrm{d}_2 = 1 \cdot 1 + 1 \cdot 0 + 0 \cdot 0 = 1$.

Compute magnitudes: $\|\mathrm{d}_1\| = \sqrt{1^2 + 1^2 + 0^2} = \sqrt{2}$, $\|\mathrm{d}_2\| = \sqrt{1^2 + 0^2 + 0^2} = 1$.

So $\cos \theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} \cdot 1} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, giving $\theta = rccos\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = 45^{{}^{\circ}}$.

The angle between the lines is $45^{{}^{\circ}}$.

The correct choice is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

65568.text: A series LCR circuit is connected to an a.c. source of $220$ V, $50$ Hz. 65568.sol:
The impedance of the series LCR circuit is given by

$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_C - X_L)^2}$

Substituting the given values:

$Z = \sqrt{80^2 + (130 - 70)^2}$

$Z = \sqrt{80^2 + 60^2}$

$Z = \sqrt{6400 + 3600} = \sqrt{10000} = 100\,\Omega$

The power factor of the circuit is

$\cos \phi = \dfrac{R}{Z}$

$\cos \phi = \dfrac{80}{100} = \dfrac{8}{10}$

Comparing this with $\dfrac{x}{10}$, we get $x = 8$.

Answer: $8$

65877.subject: Physics
65877.text: The number of revolutions per second made by an electron in the first Bohr orbit of hydrogen atom is (h$ = Planck's constant, $m$ is the mass of electron and $r$ is the radius of the orbit.)$
65877.sol:
According to Bohr's quantization condition, the angular momentum of an electron in the $n$-th orbit is given by:

$mvr = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$

For the first Bohr orbit, $n = 1$:

$mvr = \dfrac{h}{2\pi}$

The velocity of the electron is:

$v = \dfrac{h}{2\pi mr}$

The number of revolutions per second (frequency $f$) is given by the ratio of velocity to the circumference of the orbit:

$f = \dfrac{v}{2\pi r}$

Substituting the value of $v$ into the frequency equation:

$f = \dfrac{\dfrac{h}{2\pi mr}}{2\pi r} = \dfrac{h}{4\pi^2 mr^2}$

Answer: $h / 4\pi^2 mr^2$

66547.text: In photoelectric effect experiment, if the frequency of incident radiation (v$) is increased, keeping all other factors constant, the stopping potential, (v > v_0$) (v_0$ = threshold frequency)$
66547.sol:
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons is given by:

$K_{\max} = h v - \Phi$

where $h$ is Planck's constant, $v$ is the frequency of incident radiation, and $\Phi$ is the work function of the material.

The stopping potential $V_0$ is related to the maximum kinetic energy by:

$e V_0 = K_{\max}$

Substituting this into the photoelectric equation gives:

$e V_0 = h v - \Phi$

$V_0 = \dfrac{h}{e} v - \dfrac{\Phi}{e}$

From this linear relationship, it is evident that the stopping potential $V_0$ increases as the frequency of incident radiation $v$ increases.

Answer: increases

67383.text: An ideal gas at pressure 'P' and temperature 'T' is enclosed in a vessel of volume 'V'. Some gas leaks through a hole from the vessel and the pressure of the enclosed gas falls to $P^1$. 67383.sol:
Initial number of moles of the gas is given by the ideal gas equation:

$n_1 = \dfrac{PV}{RT}$

After the leakage, the final number of moles of the gas is:

$n_2 = \dfrac{P^1V}{RT}$

The number of moles of the gas that have leaked is:

$\Delta n = n_1 - n_2$

$\Delta n = \dfrac{PV}{RT} - \dfrac{P^1V}{RT}$

$\Delta n = \dfrac{V}{RT}(P - P^1)$

Answer: $\dfrac{V}{RT}(P - P^1)$

68137.text: A vessel completely filled with water has two holes 'P' and 'Q' at depths ' 2 h ' and ' 8 h ' from the top respectively. 68137.sol:
Torricelli's Law states that the velocity of efflux from an orifice at depth $h$ is $v = \sqrt{2gh}$. The volume flow rate is given by $A v$.

For hole P at depth $2h$, the velocity is $v_P = \sqrt{2g(2h)} = 2\sqrt{gh}$. Its area is $A_P = a^2$.

For hole Q at depth $8h$, the velocity is $v_Q = \sqrt{2g(8h)} = 4\sqrt{gh}$. Its area is $A_Q = \pi r^2$.

Equating the volume flow rates:

$a^2 \cdot 2\sqrt{gh} = \pi r^2 \cdot 4\sqrt{gh}$

Dividing both sides by $2\sqrt{gh}$ gives:

$a^2 = 2\pi r^2$

Thus, $a = r\sqrt{2\pi}$, corresponding to option B.

68954.subject: Physics
68954.text: When a beam of white light is allowed to pass through convex lens parallel to principle axis, the different colors of light converge at different point on the principle axis after refraction. This is called
68954.sol:
The refractive index of the material of a lens varies with the wavelength of light. According to Cauchy's formula, the refractive index is different for different colors of white light.

The focal length of a lens is given by the lens maker's formula: $\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1) \left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right).

Since $\mu$ is different for different colors, the focal length $f$ will also be different for different colors. As a result, when a beam of white light passes through a convex lens parallel to the principal axis, the different colors converge at different points on the principal axis.

This inability of a lens to focus all colors of light at a single point is known as chromatic aberration.

Answer: chromatic aberration$

69728.text: What will be the ratio of rate of radiation of metal sphere at two different temperatures $T_1 = 527^{}^{\circ}$ C and $T_2 = 127^{}^{\circ}$ C
69728.sol:
The temperatures in Kelvin are given by:

$T_1 = 527 + 273 = 800 \text{ K}$

$T_2 = 127 + 273 = 400 \text{ K}$

According to the Stefan-Boltzmann law, the rate of radiation $E$ is proportional to the fourth power of the absolute temperature $T$:

$E \propto T^4$

Taking the ratio of the rates of radiation at the two temperatures:

69821.text: Two uniform brass rods A and B of length ' $l$ ' and ' $2 l$ ' and their radii ' $2 \mathrm{r}$ ' and ' $\mathrm{r}$ ' respectively are heated to same temperature. The ratio of the increase in the volume of $\operatorname{rod} \mathrm{A}$ to that of $\operatorname{rod} \mathrm{B}$ is

69952.subject: Physics
69952.text: A polyatomic gas at pressure 'P', having volume 'V' expands isothermally to a volume ' 3 V ' and then adiabatically to a volume ' 24 V '. The final pressure of gas is (for moderate temperature changes)
69952.sol:
The gas undergoes isothermal expansion from volume $V$ to $3V$ at constant temperature. Since $PV = \text{constant}$ for isothermal processes, the pressure reduces from $P$ to $P_2 = P \cdot \frac{V}{3V} = \frac{P}{3}$.

The subsequent adiabatic expansion from volume $3V$ to $24V$ follows $PV^\gamma = \text{constant}$, with $\gamma = \frac{4}{3}$ for polyatomic gases. Using $P_2(3V)^{4/3} = P_3(24V)^{4/3}$:

$P_3 = \frac{P}{3} \cdot \left(\frac{3V}{24V}\right)^{4/3} = \frac{P}{3} \cdot \left(\frac{1}{8}\right)^{4/3} = \frac{P}{3} \cdot \frac{1}{2^{3 \cdot (4/3)}} = \frac{P}{3} \cdot \frac{1}{16} = \frac{P}{48}$

Final pressure: $\frac{P}{48}$

71208.subject: Biology
71208.text: Which of the following layers covering the secondary follicle is fibrous?
71208.sol:
During the development of the ovarian follicle, the primary follicle matures into a secondary follicle. At this stage, the theca layer differentiates into two distinct layers: the inner theca interna and the outer theca externa.

The theca interna is a cellular, highly vascularized, and glandular layer responsible for secreting androgens.

The theca externa is the outermost layer and is composed of fibrous connective tissue containing fibroblasts and collagen. Therefore, the theca externa is the fibrous layer covering the secondary follicle.

Answer: Theca externa

72150.subject: Physics
72150.text:
A student plots two different graphs using the same photoelectric experiment data.
1. Maximum kinetic energy (K_\max$) against frequency (\nu$)
2. Stopping potential (V_o$) against frequency (\nu$)
Let the slope of graph 1 be $S_1$ and the slope of graph 2 be $S_2$.
What is the relationship between the slopes?
(h = Planck's constant, e = charge on electron)
72150.sol:
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation:

$K_\max = h u - \Phi$

Comparing this with the equation of a straight line $y = mx + c$, the slope of the $K_\max$ versus $ u$ graph is:

$S_1 = h$

The stopping potential $V_o$ is related to maximum kinetic energy by $K_\max = eV_o$. Substituting this in the photoelectric equation:

$eV_o = h u - \Phi$

$V_o = \dfrac{h}{e} u - \dfrac{\Phi}{e}$

Comparing this with the equation of a straight line, the slope of the $V_o$ versus $ u$ graph is:

$S_2 = \dfrac{h}{e}$

Taking the ratio of the two slopes:

$\dfrac{S_1}{S_2} = \dfrac{h}{\dfrac{h}{e}} = e$

Answer: $\dfrac{S_1}{S_2} = e$

72405.subject: Physics
72405.text: If the radiant heat absorbed by the body is $75\%$ of the incident heat and if the coefficient of the reflection is $0.15$, then the coefficient of transmission is
72405.sol:
Let the total incident heat be $Q$.

The radiant heat absorbed by the body is $75\%$ of the incident heat. Therefore, the coefficient of absorption is $a = 0.75$.

The coefficient of reflection is given as $r = 0.15$.

According to the conservation of energy, the sum of the coefficients of absorption, reflection, and transmission is equal to $1$.

$a + r + t = 1$

Substituting the given values:

$0.75 + 0.15 + t = 1$

$0.90 + t = 1$

$t = 1 - 0.90 = 0.10$

The coefficient of transmission is $0.10$.

Answer: $0.10$

77611.subject: Mathematics
77611.text: What is $\lim\limits_{x\to1}\dfrac{x^{(n^2-1)}-1}{x^{(n+1)}-1}$ equal to, where $n > 1$ is a natural number ?
77611.sol:
The given limit is $\lim\limits_{x\to1}\dfrac{x^{(n^2-1)}-1}{x^{(n+1)}-1}$.

As $x \to 1$, the expression takes the indeterminate form $\dfrac{0}{0}$.

Applying L'Hospital's rule, we differentiate the numerator and the denominator with respect to $x$:

$\lim\limits_{x\to1}\dfrac{(n^2-1)x^{n^2-2}}{(n+1)x^n}$

Substituting $x=1$, we get:

$\dfrac{n^2-1}{n+1}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{(n-1)(n+1)}{n+1}$

$\Rightarrow n-1$

Answer: $n-1$

77621.text: If $f(x)=\frac{x 2+x+|x|}{x}$ then what is $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} f(x)$ equal to?

80342.subject: Botany
80342.text: The morphological nature of the edible part of coconut is
80342.sol:
The edible part of coconut is endosperm. Coconut water is free nuclear endosperm and the white kernel is the cellular endosperm.

Initially, the coconut is a nuclear liquid endosperm. it is a coenocytic liquid tissue with lots of rapidly dividing nuclei. At some point, gelification of the soil surrounding the nuclei occurs and cellular boundaries start to appear. These cells and nuclei start to settle down on the endothelium (inner lining of the integuments) and the cells divide to produce a columnar sort of a covering over it. This is what forms the characteristic of coconut meat. Development of the cellular endosperm is by coalescence of these deposited cells and nuclei at the antipodal end and continues towards the top. The cells right above the endothelium stay meristematic for a long time while the columnar cells on top of this meristematic layer grow radially inward.

80476.subject: Botany
80476.text: Which one of the following is a triploid cell ?
80476.sol:
Synergids are haploid ($n$) cells present in the embryo sac.

The central cell contains two polar nuclei ($n + n$) which fuse to form a diploid secondary nucleus ($2n$).

The zygote is a diploid ($2n$) cell formed by the fusion of a male gamete ($n$) with the egg cell ($n$).

The primary endosperm cell is formed by the fusion of a male gamete ($n$) with the two polar nuclei or secondary nucleus ($2n$) of the central cell. This process is called triple fusion, resulting in a triploid ($3n$) primary endosperm cell.

Answer: Primary endosperm cell

83481.subject: Physics
83481.text:
The current $I$ in the circuit shown below is :
(All diodes are ideal and identical)
83481.sol:
From the given circuit, the positive terminal of the $10\text{ V}$ battery is connected to the left side of the parallel branches.

Therefore, the left side is at a higher potential compared to the right side.

The diodes in the branches with $4\ \Omega$ and $2\ \Omega$ resistors have their anodes connected to the higher potential side, so they are forward-biased and act as short circuits (since they are ideal).

The diodes in the branches with $3\ \Omega$ and $5\ \Omega$ resistors have their cathodes connected to the higher potential side, so they are reverse-biased and act as open circuits.

The effective circuit consists of the $4\ \Omega$ and $2\ \Omega$ resistors connected in parallel across the $10\text{ V}$ battery.

The equivalent resistance of the circuit is:

$R_{eq} = \dfrac{4 \times 2}{4 + 2} = \dfrac{8}{6} = \dfrac{4}{3}\ \Omega$

The total current $I$ in the circuit is:

$I = \dfrac{V}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{10}{\dfrac{4}{3}} = \dfrac{30}{4} = \dfrac{15}{2}\text{ A}$

Answer: $\dfrac{15}{2}$ A

84263.sol: Adrenaline (epinephrine) is a hormone produced by the adrenal medulla and is secreted in great amounts during emotional stress. It elevates the glucose level in the blood stream (by glycogenolysis) which is accompanied by an increase in oxygen consumption, body temperature and heat production. 90075.text: The lengths of the tangents from any point on the circle $x^{2} + y^{2} + 8x + 1 = 0$ to the circles $x^{2} + y^{2} + 7x + 1 = 0$ and $x^{2} + y^{2} + 4x + 1 = 0$ are in the ratio

Let the point on $x^{2} + y^{2} + 8x + 1 = 0$~is $\left(h, k\right)$

93291.text: How many time faster than the present speed would the earth have to rotate about its axis so that the apparent weight of the bodies on the equator becomes zero? (The radius of the earth $R = 6.4 \times {10}^{6}m$)
93291.sol:
Let ${\omega}_{0}$ be the new angular velocity.

At the equator ${g}_{E} = g - R{\omega}^{2}$

The weight $m{g}_{E}$ should be zero. ${g}_{E} = 0$

$∴ R{\omega}_{0}^{2} = g$ or ${\omega}_{0} = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{R}}$

$∴ {\omega}_{0} = \sqrt{\dfrac{9.8}{6.4 \times 1{0}^{6}}} = 1.24 \times 1{0}^{- 3}\dfrac{rad}{s}$

The present angular velocity of the earth is $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} = \dfrac{2 \times 3.14}{24 \times 60 \times 60}$

$∴\omega = \dfrac{3.14 \times 1{0}^{- 2}}{12 \times 36} = 7.27 \times 1{0}^{- 5}$

$∴ \dfrac{{\omega}_{0}}{\omega} = \dfrac{1.24 \times 1{0}^{- 3}}{7.27 \times 1{0}^{- 5}} = 17$

$∴ {\omega}_{0} = 17\omega$

It should rotate faster by 17 times the present value.

93762.sol:
The surface energy of a bubble

$E$ = Tension $\times$ surface area

$E = T \times A$

For soap bubble

$E = 2T \times A$

$E = 2T \times 4\piR^{2}$

Here, $R$ = radius of the bubble

If the radius is doubled then we have

$E^{′} = 2T \times 4\piR^{2}$

$E^{′} = 2T \times 4\pi\left(2R\right)^{2}$

$E^{′} = 32\piR^{2}T$

Work done = $E ' - E$

$⇒ 32\piR^{2}T - 8\piR^{2}T = 24\piR^{2}T$

putting the value of x in equation (1)

95240.subject: Botany
95240.text: Select the INCORRECT statement regarding the anatomy of a typical monocotyledonous stem
options: Vascular bundles are scattered, conjoint, collateral and closed.
Each vascular bundle is surrounded by a bundle sheath.
Ground tissue is differentiated into cortex, endodermis, pericycle and pith.
95240.sol:
Monocotyledons are the plant group of Angiosperms that have one embryonic leaf (cotyledon) in their seed.

The stem of monocot is quite different from that of a dicot. The stem has no cambium, as a result, secondary growth is absent. The vascular bundles in it are scattered unlike in dicot. They are also conjoint, collateral, and closed. The hypodermis of monocot stem is made of sclerenchymatous tissue and the vascular bundles are surrounded by bundle sheath of the same tissue. In it, phloem parenchyma is absent. Ground tissue is mainly parenchymatous and not differentiated into cortex, pericycle, and pith as the vascular bundles are scattered in it.

100030.subject: Physics
100030.text: In an experiment to determine the acceleration due to gravity ($g$) using a simple pendulum, a student measures the length of the pendulum as $(100.0 \pm 0.1) \text{ cm}$ and the time period as $(2.00 \pm 0.02) \text{ s}$. The maximum percentage error in the measurement of $g$ will be:
100030.sol:
The acceleration due to gravity $g$ determined by a simple pendulum is given by $g = \dfrac{4\pi^2 L}{T^2}$.

The maximum percentage error in $g$ is given by the sum of the fractional errors of the individual quantities, taking into account their powers:

$\dfrac{\Delta g}{g} \times 100 = \dfrac{\Delta L}{L} \times 100 + 2 \left( \dfrac{\Delta T}{T} \times 100 \right)$

Given $L = (100.0 \pm 0.1) \text{ cm}$ and $T = (2.00 \pm 0.02) \text{ s}$, we calculate the individual percentage errors:

Percentage error in $L = \left( \dfrac{0.1}{100.0} \right) \times 100 = 0.1\%$

Percentage error in $T = \left( \dfrac{0.02}{2.00} \right) \times 100 = 1.0\%$

Substituting these into the error equation:

Maximum percentage error in $g = 0.1\% + 2(1.0\%) = 2.1\%$

Answer: $2.1\%$

100350.subject: Physics
100350.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If a car travels between two cities covering the journey in two equal distance halves at speeds $v_1$ and $v_2$ (where $v_1 \neq v_2$), its average speed is always less than if it had traveled at those same speeds for two equal time intervals.

Reason (R): The average speed for a journey divided into two equal distance halves is given by the arithmetic mean of the two speeds.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
100350.sol:
For a journey divided into two equal distance halves at speeds $v_1$ and $v_2$, the average speed is the harmonic mean: $v_{dist} = \dfrac{2v_1v_2}{v_1 + v_2}$.

For a journey divided into two equal time intervals at speeds $v_1$ and $v_2$, the average speed is the arithmetic mean: $v_{time} = \dfrac{v_1 + v_2}{2}$.

Mathematically, for any two distinct positive numbers, the harmonic mean is strictly less than the arithmetic mean ($v_{dist} < v_{time}$). Therefore, the Assertion (A) is true.

The Reason (R) states that the average speed for equal distance halves is the arithmetic mean, which is incorrect. It is the harmonic mean. Thus, Reason (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

100901.subject: Physics
100901.text: A particle of mass $1 \text{ kg}$, initially at rest at the origin, is acted upon by a two-dimensional variable force given by $\vec{F} = (2x \hat{i} + 3y^2 \hat{j}) \text{ N}$, where $x$ and $y$ are in metres. The speed of the particle when it reaches the coordinates $(2 \text{ m}, 2 \text{ m})$ is:
100901.sol:
The work done by a two-dimensional variable force is calculated by integrating the force components along their respective axes.

$W = \int \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r} = \int (F_x dx + F_y dy)$

Given $\vec{F} = (2x \hat{i} + 3y^2 \hat{j}) \text{ N}$, the work done from $(0,0)$ to $(2,2)$ is:
$W_x = \int_{0}^{2} 2x dx = \left[ x^2 \right]_{0}^{2} = 4 \text{ J}$
$W_y = \int_{0}^{2} 3y^2 dy = \left[ y^3 \right]_{0}^{2} = 8 \text{ J}$

Total work done, $W = W_x + W_y = 4 + 8 = 12 \text{ J}$

According to the work-energy theorem, the total work done is equal to the change in kinetic energy:
$W = \Delta K = \dfrac{1}{2} m v^2 - \dfrac{1}{2} m u^2$

Since the particle starts from rest ($u = 0$) and its mass $m = 1 \text{ kg}$:
$12 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 \times v^2$
$v^2 = 24$
$v = \sqrt{24} = 2\sqrt{6} \text{ m/s}$

Answer: $2\sqrt{6} \text{ m/s}$

102001.subject: Physics
102001.text: If one mole of an ideal gas at $\left({P}_{1}, {V}_{1}\right)$ is allowed to expand reversibly and isothermally ($A to B$) its pressure is reduced to one-half of the original pressure (see figure). This is followed by a constant volume cooling till its pressure is reduced to one-fourth of the initial value $\left(B \to C\right) .$ Then it is restored to its initial state by a reversible adiabatic compression ($C to A$). The net workdone by the gas is equal to:
102001.sol:
$A - B =$ isothermal process

${W}_{AB} = {P}_{1}{V}_{1}ln\left[\dfrac{2{V}_{1}}{{V}_{1}}\right] = {P}_{1}{V}_{1}ln\left(2\right)$

$B - C \to$ Isochoric process

${W}_{BC} = 0$

$C - A \to$Adiabatic process

${W}_{CA} = \dfrac{{P}_{1}{V}_{1} - \dfrac{{P}_{1}}{4} \times 2{V}_{1}}{1 - \gamma} = \dfrac{{P}_{1}{V}_{1}\left[1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right]}{1 - \gamma} = \dfrac{{P}_{1}{V}_{1}}{2\left(1 - \gamma\right)}$

${W}_{net} = {W}_{AB} + {W}_{BC} + {W}_{CA}\left\{{P}_{1}{V}_{1} = RT\right\}$

$= {P}_{1}{V}_{1}ln\left(2\right) + 0 + \dfrac{{P}_{1}{V}_{1}}{2\left(1 - \gamma\right)}$

${W}_{net} = RT\left[ln\left(2\right) - \dfrac{1}{2\left(\gamma - 1\right)}\right]$

102906.subject: Physics
102906.text:
An electric dipole consists of two charges $+q$ and $-q$ separated by a distance of $2\text{ cm}$. What is the work done by an external agent in moving a test charge $+Q$ slowly from a point on the equatorial plane (at a distance of $5\text{ cm}$ from the center of the dipole) to a point on the axial line at a distance of $3\text{ cm}$ from the center (on the side of the positive charge)?

(Take $K = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}$)
102906.sol:
The work done by an external agent in moving a charge $+Q$ is given by $W = Q(V_f - V_i)$, where $V_i$ and $V_f$ are the initial and final electric potentials respectively.

The initial point is on the equatorial plane of the dipole. The electric potential at any point on the equatorial plane of a dipole is zero, so $V_i = 0$.

The final point is on the axial line at a distance $r = 3\text{ cm}$ from the center, on the side of the positive charge. The length of the dipole is $2a = 2\text{ cm}$, so $a = 1\text{ cm}$.

The exact electric potential at an axial point is:
$V_f = \dfrac{Kq}{r-a} - \dfrac{Kq}{r+a}$

Substituting the given values (in meters):
$V_f = \dfrac{Kq}{(3 - 1) \times 10^{-2}} - \dfrac{Kq}{(3 + 1) \times 10^{-2}}$
$V_f = \dfrac{Kq}{2 \times 10^{-2}} - \dfrac{Kq}{4 \times 10^{-2}}$
$V_f = Kq \times 10^2 \left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{4}\right) = Kq \times 100 \times \dfrac{1}{4} = 25 Kq$

Therefore, the work done is:
$W = Q(25 Kq - 0) = 25 KqQ$

Answer: $25 KqQ$

103136.subject: Physics
103136.text: Two capacitors of capacitance $2 \mu\text{F}$ and $4 \mu\text{F}$ are connected in parallel. This combination is then connected in series with an unknown capacitor $C_3$. If the total equivalent capacitance of the entire arrangement is $3 \mu\text{F}$, what is the value of $C_3$?
103136.sol:
The equivalent capacitance of the two capacitors in parallel is:
$C_p = 2 \mu\text{F} + 4 \mu\text{F} = 6 \mu\text{F}$

This combination $C_p$ is in series with $C_3$. The total equivalent capacitance $C_{eq}$ is given as $3 \mu\text{F}$.
For capacitors in series, the formula is:
$\dfrac{1}{C_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{C_p} + \dfrac{1}{C_3}$

Substituting the known values:
$\dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{C_3}$

$\dfrac{1}{C_3} = \dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{2 - 1}{6} = \dfrac{1}{6}$

Therefore, $C_3 = 6 \mu\text{F}$.

Using the formula $C_{eq} = \dfrac{C_p \times C_3}{C_p + C_3}$ incorrectly to solve for $C_3$ as if it were the equivalent of $3$ and $6$ in series leads to the wrong answer of $2 \mu\text{F}$.

Answer: $6 \mu\text{F}$

103700.subject: Physics
103700.text: A uniform conducting wire of a given length is bent into a single-turn circular loop. When a current $I$ is passed through it, the magnetic field at its centre is $B$ and its magnetic dipole moment is $M$. If the same wire is now rewound to form a circular coil of $4$ turns and the same current $I$ is passed through it, what will be the new magnetic field at the centre and the new magnetic dipole moment, respectively?
103700.sol:
Let the total length of the uniform wire be $L$.

For the single-turn loop (initial state):
$L = 2\pi R \implies R = \dfrac{L}{2\pi}$
Magnetic field at the centre, $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$
Magnetic dipole moment, $M = I \pi R^2$

When the same wire is rewound into $n = 4$ turns (final state):
$L = 4 \times 2\pi R' \implies R' = \dfrac{R}{4}$

The new magnetic field at the centre is:
$B' = \dfrac{\mu_0 n I}{2R'} = \dfrac{\mu_0 (4) I}{2(R/4)} = 16 \left(\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R}\right) = 16B$

The new magnetic dipole moment is:
$M' = n I \pi (R')^2 = 4 I \pi \left(\dfrac{R}{4}\right)^2 = \dfrac{4}{16} I \pi R^2 = \dfrac{1}{4} (I \pi R^2) = \dfrac{M}{4}$

Therefore, the new magnetic field is $16B$ and the new magnetic dipole moment is $\dfrac{M}{4}$.

Answer: $16B$ and $\dfrac{M}{4}$

105564.subject: Physics
105564.text: Two monochromatic light beams of photon energies $4 \mathrm{eV}$ and $7 \mathrm{eV}$ are incident sequentially on the same metal surface. If the ratio of the maximum speeds of the emitted photoelectrons is $1 : 2$ respectively, the work function of the metal is:
105564.sol:
Let the work function of the metal be $\phi$.
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy is $K_{\max} = E - \phi$.

For the two incident beams, the maximum kinetic energies are:
$K_1 = 4 \mathrm{eV} - \phi$
$K_2 = 7 \mathrm{eV} - \phi$

The kinetic energy is proportional to the square of the maximum speed ($K \propto v^2$). Therefore, the ratio of their kinetic energies is:

$\dfrac{K_1}{K_2} = \left(\dfrac{v_1}{v_2}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Substituting the expressions for $K_1$ and $K_2$:

$\dfrac{4 - \phi}{7 - \phi} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Cross-multiplying yields:

$16 - 4\phi = 7 - \phi$
$3\phi = 9$
$\phi = 3 \mathrm{eV}$

Answer: $3 \mathrm{eV}$

107732.subject: Chemistry
107732.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The molecule of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ has a higher dipole moment than $\mathrm{SO}_2$.

Reason (R): $\mathrm{CO}_2$ has a linear symmetrical structure, while $\mathrm{SO}_2$ has a bent structure due to the presence of a lone pair of electrons on the sulphur atom.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
107732.sol:
In $\mathrm{CO}_2$, the central carbon atom is $sp$ hybridized and has no lone pairs, resulting in a linear symmetrical geometry. The two $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$ bond dipoles are equal and opposite, cancelling each other out exactly. Thus, the net dipole moment of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is zero.

In $\mathrm{SO}_2$, the central sulphur atom is $sp^2$ hybridized and possesses one lone pair of electrons. This gives the molecule a bent (V-shaped) structure. The $\mathrm{S}=\mathrm{O}$ bond dipoles do not cancel each other, resulting in a non-zero net dipole moment.

Therefore, $\mathrm{SO}_2$ has a higher dipole moment than $\mathrm{CO}_2$. Assertion (A) is incorrect, while Reason (R) is correct.

Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

108674.subject: Chemistry
108674.text: For a reversible reaction $\text{X} \rightleftharpoons \text{Y}$, the standard enthalpy change ($\Delta H^\circ$) is $400$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ and the standard entropy change ($\Delta S^\circ$) is $800$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$. Assuming $\Delta H^\circ$ and $\Delta S^\circ$ are independent of temperature, the temperature in $^\circ\text{C}$ at which the equilibrium mixture contains equal moles of $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$ is:
108674.sol:
For the reaction $\text{X} \rightleftharpoons \text{Y}$, the equilibrium constant is $K = \dfrac{[\text{Y}]}{[\text{X}]}$.

When the equilibrium mixture contains equal moles of $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$, their concentrations are equal, meaning $K = 1$.

The standard Gibbs free energy change is given by $\Delta G^\circ = -RT \ln K$. For $K = 1$, $\Delta G^\circ = 0$.

Using the Gibbs-Helmholtz equation $\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T \Delta S^\circ$, we have:
$\Delta H^\circ = T \Delta S^\circ$

Given $\Delta H^\circ = 400$ kJ mol$^{-1} = 400000$ J mol$^{-1}$ and $\Delta S^\circ = 800$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$.

Solving for temperature $T$ in Kelvin:
$T = \dfrac{\Delta H^\circ}{\Delta S^\circ} = \dfrac{400000}{800} = 500$ K

Converting the temperature to Celsius:
$T (\text{in } ^\circ\text{C}) = 500 - 273 = 227$ $^\circ\text{C}$

Answer: $227$

114368.subject: Chemistry
114368.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The plots of $\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}$ versus $\sqrt{c}$ for aqueous solutions of $\mathrm{BaCl}_2$ and $\mathrm{MgSO}_4$ have the same slope at $298\mathrm{~K}$.
Reason (R): $\mathrm{BaCl}_2$ is a 2-1 electrolyte while $\mathrm{MgSO}_4$ is a 2-2 electrolyte, hence they have different values for the constant '$A$' in the Debye-Hückel-Onsager equation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
114368.sol:
The variation of molar conductivity ($\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}$) with concentration for strong electrolytes is given by $\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}} = \Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ} - A\sqrt{c}$.

The slope of the $\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}$ versus $\sqrt{c}$ plot is $-A$. The value of the constant '$A$' depends on the type of electrolyte, which is determined by the valency of the cation and anion produced on dissociation.

$\mathrm{BaCl}_2$ dissociates into $\mathrm{Ba}^{2+}$ and $2\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$, making it a 2-1 electrolyte.
$\mathrm{MgSO}_4$ dissociates into $\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}$, making it a 2-2 electrolyte.

Since they are different types of electrolytes, they have different values for the constant '$A$'. Therefore, their plots will have different slopes.

Thus, Assertion (A) is not correct, but Reason (R) is correct.

Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

114880.subject: Chemistry
114880.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For a given rise in temperature, a reaction with a higher activation energy shows a greater percentage increase in its rate constant compared to a reaction with a lower activation energy.

Reason (R): The rate constant of a chemical reaction is directly proportional to its activation energy.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
114880.sol:
From the Arrhenius equation, the relationship between rate constants at two temperatures is:

$\log \left(\dfrac{k_2}{k_1}\right) = \dfrac{E_a}{2.303 R} \left(\dfrac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2}\right)$

For a constant temperature interval ($T_2 - T_1$), the value of $\log(k_2/k_1)$ is directly proportional to the activation energy ($E_a$). Therefore, a reaction with a higher $E_a$ will have a larger ratio of $k_2/k_1$, meaning it exhibits a greater percentage increase in its rate constant. Thus, the Assertion (A) is true.

According to the Arrhenius equation, $k = A e^{-E_a/RT}$. This indicates that the rate constant decreases exponentially as the activation energy increases. It is not directly proportional to the activation energy. Thus, the Reason (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

117060.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Terbium (IV) acts as an oxidant in aqueous solution.

Reason (R): The $+4$ oxidation state of Terbium is favoured by its noble gas core electronic configuration.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
117060.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct: Terbium (Tb) can show a $+4$ oxidation state, but the most stable oxidation state for all lanthanoids is $+3$. Thus, $Tb^{4+}$ readily accepts an electron to become $Tb^{3+}$, acting as a strong oxidant in aqueous solutions.

Reason (R) is incorrect: The atomic number of Terbium is $65$. The electronic configuration of Tb is $[Xe] 4f^{9} 6s^{2}$. In the $+4$ oxidation state, the configuration of $Tb^{4+}$ is $[Xe] 4f^{7}$. This represents a stable half-filled $f$-subshell, not a noble gas core configuration (which would be $4f^{0}$, as seen in $Ce^{4+}$).

Therefore, Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.

Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.

117097.subject: Chemistry
117097.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): $\mathrm{Cu}^{+}$ and $\mathrm{Sc}^{3+}$ both exhibit a spin-only magnetic moment of zero.
Reason (R): Both ions lack unpaired electrons due to a completely filled $3d$ subshell.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
117097.sol:
Assertion (A): The electronic configuration of $\mathrm{Cu}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^{10} 4s^1$. Thus, $\mathrm{Cu}^{+}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^{10}$. It has 0 unpaired electrons, so its magnetic moment is zero.
The electronic configuration of $\mathrm{Sc}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^1 4s^2$. Thus, $\mathrm{Sc}^{3+}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^0$. It also has 0 unpaired electrons, so its magnetic moment is zero.
Therefore, the Assertion is true.

Reason (R): While $\mathrm{Cu}^{+}$ lacks unpaired electrons because of a completely filled $3d$ subshell ($3d^{10}$), $\mathrm{Sc}^{3+}$ lacks unpaired electrons because it has an empty $3d$ subshell ($3d^0$).
Therefore, the Reason is false.

Answer: Assertion is true but Reason is false.

123230.subject: Botany
123230.text: What is the location of the pericycle in a dicot stem?
options: Between the epidermis and the cortex
Between the endodermis and the phloem
123230.sol: The transverse section of a typical young dicotyledonous stem shows that the epidermis is the outermost protective layer of the stem Covered with a thin layer of cuticle, it may bear trichomes and a few stomata. The cells arranged in multiple layers between epidermis and pericycle constitute the cortex. It consists of three sub-zones. The outer hypodermis, consists of a few layers of collenchymatous cells just below the epidermis, which provide mechanical strength to the young stem. Cortical layers below hypodermis consist of rounded thin walled parenchymatous cells with conspicuous intercellular spaces. The innermost layer of the cortex is called the endodermis. The cells of the endodermis are rich in starch grains and the layer is also referred to as the starch sheath. Pericycle is present on the inner side of the endodermis and above the phloem in the form of semi-lunar patches of sclerenchyma. In between the vascular bundles there are a few layers of radially placed parenchymatous cells, which constitute medullary rays. A large number of vascular bundles are arranged in a ring ; the ‘ring’ arrangement of vascular bundles is a characteristic of dicot stem. Each vascular bundle is conjoint, open, and with endarch protoxylem. A large number of rounded, parenchymatous cells with large intercellularspaces which occupy the central portion of the stem constitute the pith.

123505.sol:
Histogen theory for shoot apical meristem has been proposed by Hanstein (1870). It advocates that there are three distinct meristematic zones (layers) called dermatogen periblem and plerome. The dermatogen is the outermost histogen giving rise to epidermis, periblem is the middle on producing the cortex and plerome is the innermost resulting in central cylinder (i.e., vascular tissue).
Cork cambium (phellogen) is the secondary lateral meristem found in outer cortical region. Its cells divide periclinally cutting off cells towards the outside (forming cork or phellem) and inside (forming secondary cortex or phelloderm).

125455.subject: Botany
125455.text: Where is the 3-carbon molecule transported after being released in the bundle sheath cells?
125455.sol: The primary CO2 acceptor is a 3-carbon molecule phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP) and is present in the mesophyll cells. The enzyme responsible for this fixation is PEP carboxylase or PEPcase. It is important to register that the mesophyll cells lack RuBisCO enzyme. The C4 acid OAA is formed in the mesophyll cells. It then forms other 4-carbon compounds like malic acid or aspartic acid in the mesophyll cells itself, which are transported to the bundle sheath cells. In the bundle sheath cells these C4 acids are broken down to release CO2 and a 3-carbon molecule. The 3-carbon molecule is transported back to the mesophyll where it is converted to PEP again, thus, completing the cycle.

128322.subject: Zoology
128322.text: What are the number of parathyroid glands present in the human body?
128322.sol: In humans, four parathyroid glands are present on the back side of the thyroid gland, one pair each in the two lobes of the thyroid gland (Figure19.3 b). The parathyroid glands secrete a peptide hormone called parathyroid hormone (PTH). The secretion of PTH is regulated by the circulating levels of calcium ions.Parathyroid hormone (PTH) increases the Ca2+ levels in the blood. PTH acts on bones and stimulates the process of bone resorption (dissolution/ demineralisation). PTH also stimulates reabsorption of Ca2+ by the renal tubules and increases Ca2+ absorption from the digested food. It is, thus, clear that PTH is a hypercalcemic hormone, i.e., it increases the blood Ca2+ levels. Along with TCT, it plays a significant role in calcium balance in the body.

128891.subject: Zoology
128891.text: What is the name of the sequential event in the heart that is cyclically repeated?
128891.sol: This sequential event in the heart which is cyclically repeated is called the cardiac cycle and it consists of systole and diastole of both the atria and ventricles. As mentioned earlier, the heart beats 72 times per minute, i.e., that many cardiac cycles are performed per minute. From this it could be deduced that the duration of a cardiac cycle is 0.8 seconds. During a cardiac cycle, each ventricle pumps out approximately 70 mL of blood which is called the stroke volume. The stroke volume multiplied by the heart rate (no. of beats per min.) gives the cardiac output. Therefore, the cardiac output can be defined as the volume of blood pumped out by each ventricle per minute and averages 5000 mL or 5 litres in a healthy individual. The body has the ability to alter the stroke volume as well as the heart rate and thereby the cardiac output.

130059.text:
Read the following statements carefully.

I. Normal expiration involves the relaxation of the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles.
II. Humans have the ability to increase the strength of inspiration and expiration with the help of additional muscles in the abdomen.
III. Inspiration occurs when the intrapulmonary pressure is higher than the atmospheric pressure.
IV. An increase in pulmonary volume leads to an increase in the intrapulmonary pressure.

How many of the above statements are correct?
130059.sol:
Statement I is correct. Normal expiration is a passive process that occurs due to the relaxation of the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles, which reduces thoracic volume.

Statement II is correct. We have the ability to increase the strength of inspiration and expiration with the help of additional muscles in the abdomen.

Statement III is incorrect. Inspiration occurs when the intrapulmonary pressure is less than the atmospheric pressure (negative pressure in the lungs).

Statement IV is incorrect. According to the principles of breathing, an increase in pulmonary volume decreases the intrapulmonary pressure, which forces air from outside to move into the lungs.

Thus, exactly two statements (I and II) are correct.

Answer: Two

130080.subject: Zoology
130080.text:
A healthy adult individual undergoes a pulmonary function test. The following respiratory values are recorded:

Total Lung Capacity (TLC) = $5800\text{ mL}$
Residual Volume (RV) = $1200\text{ mL}$
Inspiratory Capacity (IC) = $3500\text{ mL}$

Based on the given data, what is the value of the Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV) for this individual?
130080.sol:
Total Lung Capacity (TLC) is the total volume of air accommodated in the lungs at the end of a forced inspiration. It is the sum of Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV), Tidal Volume (TV), Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV), and Residual Volume (RV).

Since Inspiratory Capacity (IC) is the sum of IRV and TV, the formula for TLC can be written as:
$\text{TLC} = \text{IC} + \text{ERV} + \text{RV}$

Given:
$\text{TLC} = 5800\text{ mL}$
$\text{IC} = 3500\text{ mL}$
$\text{RV} = 1200\text{ mL}$

Substituting the values:
$5800 = 3500 + \text{ERV} + 1200$
$5800 = 4700 + \text{ERV}$
$\text{ERV} = 5800 - 4700 = 1100\text{ mL}$

Calculating $\text{TLC} - \text{IC}$ alone gives the Functional Residual Capacity ($2300\text{ mL}$), and $\text{TLC} - \text{RV}$ gives the Vital Capacity ($4600\text{ mL}$).

Answer: $1100\text{ mL}$

Assertion (A) is correct because oogenesis is indeed a discontinuous process with prolonged meiotic arrests, unlike spermatogenesis which is a continuous process beginning at puberty.

Reason (R) is correct and provides the exact mechanism for this discontinuity: primary oocytes arrest in prophase-I during fetal life and only resume meiosis starting at puberty, and the resulting secondary oocytes arrest in metaphase-II, completing meiosis only if fertilization occurs.

Thus, Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

(i) Prostrate gland
(ii) Seminal vesicle
(iii) Bulbourethral gland
131320.sol: Seminal vesicles produce an alkaline secretion which forms $60 \%$ of the volume of semen. The secretion of the seminal vesicles contains fructose, prostaglandins, citrate, inositol, and clotting proteins. Prostate gland produces a milky and slightly alkaline secretion which forms $25 \%$ of the volume of semen. It possesses calcium, phosphate, bicarbonate, enzymes prefibrolysin, clotting enzymes, and prostaglandins. Bulbourethral glands or Cowper's glands also secrete an alkaline fluid which neutralizes acids from urine in the urethera. Their secretion contributes the least to semen but is very important.

131424.subject: Zoology
131424.text: What is the length of a DNA double helix in a typical mammalian cell?
131424.sol: Taken the distance between two consecutive base pairs as 0.34 nm (0.34×10–9 m), if the length of DNA double helix in a typical mammalian cell is calculated (simply by multiplying the total number of bp with distance between two consecutive bp, that is, 6.6 × $10^{9}$ bp × 0.34 × 10-9m/bp), it comes out to be approximately 2.2 meters. A length that is far greater than the dimension of a typical nucleus (approximately 10–6 m). How is such a long polymer packaged in a cell? If the length of E. coli DNA is 1.36 mm, can you calculate the number of base pairs in E.coli? In prokaryotes, such as, E. coli, though they do not have a defined nucleus, the DNA is not scattered throughout the cell. DNA (being negatively charged) is held with some proteins (that have positive charges) in a region termed as ‘nucleoid’. The DNA in a nucleoid is organized in large loops held by proteins.
131424.meta: What is the length of a DNA double helix in a typical mammalian cell?

131492.subject: Zoology
131492.text: How much time does E. coli take to complete the process of replication?
131492.sol: In living cells, such as E. coli, the process of replication requires a set of catalysts (enzymes). The main enzyme is referred to as DNA-dependent DNA polymerase, since it uses a DNA template to catalyze the polymerisation of deoxynucleotides. These enzymes are highly efficient enzymes as they have to catalyze polymerisation of a large number of nucleotides in a very short time. E. coli that has only 4.6 ×106 bp (compare it with humans whose diploid content is 6.6 × 109 bp), completes the process of replication within 18 minutes; that means the average rate of polymerisation has to be approximately 2000 bp per second. Not only do these polymerases have to be fast, but they also have to catalyze the reaction with a high degree of accuracy. Any mistake during replication would result in mutations. Furthermore, energetically replication is a very expensive process. Deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates serve dual purposes
131492.meta: How much time does E. coli take to complete the process of replication?

131588.subject: Zoology
131588.text: Which gene codes for the repressor of the lac operon?
131588.sol: The lac operon consists of one regulatory gene (the i gene – here the term i does not refer to inducer, rather it is derived from the word inhibitor) and three structural genes (z, y, and a). The i gene codes for the repressor of the lac operon. The z gene codes for beta-galactosidase (β-gal), which is primarily responsible for the hydrolysis of the disaccharide, lactose into its monomeric units, galactose and glucose. The y gene codes for permease, which increases permeability of the cell to β-galactosides. The gene encodes a transacetylase. Hence, all the three gene products in lac operon are required for metabolism of lactose. In most other operons as well, the genes present in the operon are needed together to function in the same or related metabolic pathway
